summary: Jardines Del Rey Airport (CCC/MUCC) serves the Jardines del Rey archipelago off Cuba's northern coast, functioning as the main gateway to the popular resort islands of Cayo Coco and Cayo Guillermo. Situated on Cayo Coco itself, the airport primarily handles international tourist flights, connecting this beach destination with Canada, Europe, and other Caribbean hubs. Its name, meaning 'Gardens of the King,' reflects the area's pristine natural beauty and status as a protected ecological reserve.
faqs:
Q: How far is Jardines Del Rey Airport from Cayo Coco resort area?
A: The airport is located on Cayo Coco itself, approximately 15-20 minutes by road from most resort hotels in the area.

Q: Are there currency exchange facilities at the airport?
A: Yes, there are typically CADECA (Cuban currency exchange) offices available, though it is often advisable to exchange money at official hotel rates for better rates.

Q: Do I need a visa to enter Cuba through this airport?
A: Most foreign visitors need a tourist card or visa to enter Cuba; requirements vary by nationality, so check with your nearest Cuban consulate before travel.

Q: Is there Wi-Fi available at Jardines Del Rey Airport?
A: Wi-Fi availability at Cuban airports is limited; consider purchasing an ETECSA Wi-Fi card if needed for connectivity.
transport_tips: Most visitors arrange pre-booked transfers or taxi services through their resort, as the airport primarily serves the all-inclusive hotel zone. Bus services are limited, so shared shuttles or private transfers are the most reliable options. Rental cars are available but driving in Cuba can be challenging without proper preparation and documentation.
local_tip: Pack a small amount of local currency (Cuban pesos or convertible pesos) in your carry-on for tips to porters and taxi drivers, as the resort areas are relatively remote with limited immediate ATM access upon arrival.
